pipeline_name: Kyiv–Western Border of Ukraine Gas Pipeline

validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence/classification. This row's specific length/diameter/start-year values trace to an identifiable primary source (Ukrtransgaz's own official corporate chronology) — an unusually strong provenance match for this citation-poor country. See the duplicate flag below for the unresolved overlap with P0777.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE and SPEC PROVENANCE: Ukrtransgaz's (UTG, utg.ua) own official 'Xronologiya istorychnogo rozvytku' (Chronology of a century of development) page — live site now 404s, but the page is intact on Wayback — states verbatim, translated: '1970: commissioned the trunk gas pipeline Kyiv – Western border of Ukraine (Thread I), length 183.6 km, Ø1020 mm' and '1972: commissioned the trunk gas pipeline Kyiv – Western border of Ukraine (Thread II), length 216.3 km, Ø1220 mm.' 183.6 + 216.3 = 399.90 km — an EXACT match to this row's LengthKnown, and the diameters (1020, 1220 mm) and both start years (1970, 1972) match exactly too. This is a company-primary source describing this exact named pipeline, not a generic/aggregate citation — the strongest kind of confirmation available in this country. Classification (gas transmission trunk, correctly in GGIT not a gathering/feeder line) is correct: UTG's own chronology explicitly calls it a 'магістральний газопровід' (trunk gas pipeline) and frames it as the westward continuation of the Yefremivka–Dolyna–Kyiv trunk. TIER CAVEAT: this is currently a single strong primary source for the exact 183.6/216.3/399.9 km figures — I could not find a second independent source stating these same precise figures (Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated 'КЗУ' article gives a materially different breakdown — 367 km/1020mm commissioned 1970 + 506 km/1220mm commissioned 1973 — for what it calls the same-named system, so it does NOT corroborate these numbers; see duplicate/spec cross-reference below). Tier is medium accordingly, not high, on Length/Diameter/StartYear specifically, despite the exact-match confidence.

validity.recommendation: Flag for the cluster-level redundancy adjudication pass vs P0777 ('Kyiv–Western Border Pipeline') — do not merge or delete either row unilaterally.
validity.researcher_notes: P1480 and P0777 are both named 'Kyiv–Western Border [of Ukraine] [Gas] Pipeline', both start at Kyiv, both are recorded as two strings with a 1020mm/~1970 first thread and a 1220mm/~1972-73 second thread — too specific a coincidence to be unrelated pipelines; they are almost certainly two GEM rows for pieces of the same real-world Kyiv–West Ukraine (КЗУ) trunk corridor. But the two rows' totals do not agree and, per P0777's own already-staged shard, cannot both be non-overlapping physical distances: P0777 = 522+590 = 1,112 km, ending at Uzhhorod; P1480 = 183.6+216.3 = 399.9 km (per the UTG chronology found here), with THIS row's gem.wiki page separately claiming an end point at Drozdovychi on the Ukraine/Poland border — a different corridor from Uzhhorod entirely. A third figure, Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated КЗУ article, gives 367+506 = 873 km for what it calls the identical named system. So there are THREE mutually inconsistent totals in circulation (1,112 / 873 / 399.9 km) for something called 'Kyiv–Western Border [of Ukraine]', and unlike P0777's numbers (which no independent source corroborates verbatim per its own shard), P1480's 399.9/1020,1220mm/1970,1972 figures DO have an exact primary-source match (UTG's own chronology, above) — which argues P1480 is not itself a fabrication, but that it and P0777 may be recording two different, or partially double-counted, definitions/segments of the same corridor (e.g., a narrower UTG-internal 'КЗУ' trunk designation vs. a broader 'Kyiv to the export hub at Uzhhorod' corridor that strings together multiple named trunks). I did not attempt to resolve which framing is correct — per the sweep's rule, that is a cluster-adjudication decision, not a single-row call. Also worth the adjudicator's attention: gem.wiki's claimed endpoint for THIS row (Drozdovychi, Lviv Oblast, on the Poland border) is not corroborated by any source I found and conflicts with the Uzhhorod/Bratstvo-system association that both Ukrainian Wikipedia and P0777's gem.wiki page give to the analogous second thread — Drozdovychi is also associated in current reporting with a MODERN (post-Soviet) Poland-interconnector investment project, unrelated to this 1970s Soviet-era trunk, so it may be an anachronistic/incorrect endpoint on the wiki page. This row's own sheet values do not currently include an EndLocation, so this is a caveat for the eventual location fill, not a live sheet error.

validity.recommendation: Do not add an EndLocation value (e.g. 'Drozdovychi') from gem.wiki without further independent verification — leave blank pending the P0777 cluster adjudication.
validity.researcher_notes: StartLocation='Kyiv' and both StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea='Ukraine' (i.e. a wholly domestic Ukrainian corridor, no Gazprom/Russian ownership implied) are consistent with the UTG chronology source and with the country-wide rule that Gazprom holds no stake inside Ukraine. EndLocation is currently blank on the sheet; I chose not to fill it because the only candidate value I found (gem.wiki's claim of 'Drozdovyci at the Ukraine/Poland border') is unverified and, per the duplicate note above, plausibly conflated with a distinct modern pipeline project at the same border town rather than this 1970s trunk.

fills.researcher_notes: tsoua.com's Key Facts page confirms GTSOU is the certified, currently operating gas transmission system operator of Ukraine (since 2020-01-01) — a general/system-level confirmation, not segment-specific. Interfax-Ukraine's 2020 report on a rupture-and-repair of the analogous КЗУ-1 (1020mm) thread near Chabany, Kyiv oblast, independently confirms the corridor was returned to active service within days, not decommissioned. Neither the end of Russian transit (2025-01-01) nor any other dated event found suggests this domestic-supply trunk has been taken out of service; per the country-scope note, transit cessation alone is not grounds to change Status.

UTG's chronology names this a 'газопровід' (gas pipeline) explicitly; Interfax's report on the related КЗУ-1 rupture independently describes it as a natural-gas high-pressure trunk. Fuel=Gas is correct and uncontested.

UTG's chronology dates Thread I to 1970 and Thread II to 1972, an exact match to StartYear1/StartYear2. This is a single (though primary/official) source for the precise year 1972 — I could not find a second independent source giving that exact year (Ukrainian Wikipedia's analogous second thread is dated 1973, describing what it treats as the same-named but differently-measured system — see duplicate flag). tsoua.com's own History page independently corroborates only the general window ('in 1970-74, [the Shebelynka-Kyiv trunk] was extended to the Western border'), not the specific 1972 year, so tier stays medium rather than high.

183.6 km (Thread I) + 216.3 km (Thread II) = 399.90 km exactly, per UTG's own chronology. Single primary source at exact precision; no independent second source found with matching figures (see duplicate/spec cross-reference vs P0777 and Ukrainian Wikipedia's differing 873 km total for a same-named system) — tier medium, not high.

UTG's chronology states Ø1020mm for Thread I and Ø1220mm for Thread II, matching the sheet exactly. Interfax's report independently confirms 1020mm for the related КЗУ-1 thread (giving that half of the value 2 independent sources), but I found no independent second source for the 1220mm figure specifically — tier medium overall.

UTG's chronology names Kyiv as the origin of this trunk and confirms it as a wholly-Ukrainian domestic corridor (consistent with StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Ukraine already on the sheet). EndLocation is left blank on the sheet and I did NOT propose a value for it — see the attribution/location caveat in validity: gem.wiki's claimed endpoint (Drozdovychi) is unverified and possibly conflated with an unrelated modern pipeline at the same border town.

fills.researcher_notes: Two independent sources confirm 'Gas TSO of Ukraine' LLC (GTSOU) as the certified, independent operator of Ukraine's entire gas transmission system since 1 January 2020, following Energy Community-backed unbundling from Naftogaz/Ukrtransgaz: tsoua.com's own Key Facts page and Ukrinform's independent 2019 news coverage of the Energy Community certification decision. This is a wholly domestic Ukrainian line — no Gazprom stake, correctly per the country-wide rule. GTSOU is the correct Owner1 entry (state-owned via Ministry of Finance/Energy control of the entity); this reflects the country's state-monopoly structure where the certified TSO is conventionally recorded as owner, not a separate asset-holding company.

summary: P1480 (Kyiv–Western Border of Ukraine Gas Pipeline) is a real, correctly classified domestic Ukrainian gas trunk — its 399.9km/1020,1220mm/1970,1972 values trace exactly to Ukrtransgaz's own official chronology (Wayback-verified), an unusually strong provenance match — but it is flagged as a likely DUPLICATE/overlap with P0777 (same name pattern, same diameter/vintage pattern, but three mutually inconsistent totals across sources: 1,112km / 873km / 399.9km), which needs cluster-level adjudication, not a unilateral merge; all 7 MISSING_REF units (Status, Fuel, Start, Length, Diameter, Location, Owner) were staged with verified refs (tier high on Status/Fuel/Owner, medium on Start/Length/Diameter/Location); EndLocation was deliberately left unfilled given an unverified/likely-wrong 'Drozdovychi' claim on gem.wiki.
